plain_english: Sanjaya says that Krishna, seeing Arjuna overcome with compassion and grief, spoke these words to him.
sanskrit_cite: atha dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ   sañjaya uvāca   taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭamaśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam | viṣīdantamidaṃ vākyamuvāca madhusūdanaḥ

plain_english: Krishna asks whence this faintness has come in difficulty, calling it unworthy, not heavenly, and fame-destroying, while first awakening Arjuna through worldly conduct.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   kutastvā kaśmalamidaṃ viṣame samupasthitam | anāryajuṣṭamasvargyamakīrtikaramarjuna | ādau lokavyavahārāśrayeṇaiva śrībhagavānarjunaṃ pratibodhayati  kramāttu jñānaṃ kariṣyatīti ataḥ anāryajuṣṭam ityāha

plain_english: Krishna shows that Arjuna's conceit of duty is unrighteous, forbids impotence, and commands him to abandon petty heart-weakness and rise.
sanskrit_cite: klaivyādibhirnirbhartsanamabhidadhadadharme tava  dharmābhimāno'yamityādi darśayati   mā klaibyaṃ gaccha kauntena naitattvayyupapadyate | kṣudraṃ  hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa

plain_english: Arjuna asks how he can fight Bhishma and Drona with arrows in battle, calling them worship-worthy.
sanskrit_cite: arjuna uvāca   kathaṃ bhīṣmamahaṃ saṅkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana iṣubhiḥ  pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāvarisūdana

plain_english: Arjuna says it is better to live by begging than to kill great-souled teachers, and he would not enjoy blood-smeared pleasures after killing Bhishma and Drona.
sanskrit_cite: gurūnahatvā hi mahānubhāvā- ñchreyaścartuṃ bhaikṣamapīha loke | na tvarthakāmastu gurūnnihatya bhuñjīya bhogān rudhirapradigdhān | bhīṣmaṃ droṇaṃ ca ityādinā bhuñjīya bhogān ityanena ca  karmaviśeṣānu-sandhānaṃ phalaviśeṣānusandhānaṃ ca heyatayā  pūrvapakṣe sūcayati

plain_english: Arjuna says he does not know which is better, that victory over relatives would be misfortune, and that he cannot decide whether to desire victory or defeat.
sanskrit_cite: naitadvidmaḥ kataranno garīyo yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ | yāneva hatvā na jijīviṣāma- ste naḥ sthitāḥ pramukhe  dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ | naitadvidyaḥ-ityanena ca karmaviśeṣānusaṃdhānamāha | nirabhisaṃdhānaṃ tāvatkarma nopapadyate | na ca  parājayamabhisaṃdhāya yuddhe pravartate | jayo'pi cāyamanartha eva | tadāha ahatvā gurūn bhaikṣamapi cartuṃ śreyaḥ | etacca  niścetumaśakyam-kiṃ jayaṃ kāṅkṣāmaḥ kiṃ vā parājayam  jayo'pi bandhūnāṃ vināśāt

plain_english: Overcome by the fault of poverty of spirit, with a mind confused about dharma, I ask you: declare what is certainly better; I am your surrendered disciple, instruct me.
sanskrit_cite: kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi tvāṃ  dharmasaṃmūḍhacetāḥ | yacchreyaḥ syānniścitaṃ brūhi tanme  śiṣyaste'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam

plain_english: I do not see what would remove my grief, even obtaining an unrivaled prosperous kingdom on earth or lordship even over the gods.
sanskrit_cite: na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyā- dyaḥ śokamucchoṣaṇamindriyāṇām | avāpya bhūmāvasapatnamṛddhaṃ rājyaṃ surāṇāmapi cādhipatyam

plain_english: Sanjaya said: having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, Gudakesha, scorcher of foes, said he would not fight; having spoken to Govinda, he became silent.
sanskrit_cite: sañjaya uvāca   evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ parantapa | na yotsyāniti  govindamuktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha

plain_english: Hrishikesha said to him, smiling as it were, O Bharata: this sinking speech in the midst of both armies indicates that Arjuna, filled with doubt, is not withdrawn from battle on one side alone, because he says, instruct me, your surrendered one.
sanskrit_cite: tamuvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasanniva bhārata | senayorubhayormadhye  sīdamānamidaṃ vacaḥ | senayorubhayormadhye-ityanenedaṃ sūcayati-saṃśayāviṣṭo'rjuno  naikapakṣeṇa yuddhānnivṛtto yata evamāha sma-śādhi māṃ tvāṃ  prapannam iti

plain_english: Therefore, standing between knowledge and ignorance, you are instructed by the holy Lord. The holy Lord said: your inner self is struck by humanity; overcome by grief and delusion, you are seized by pity; seeing kinsmen who have approached the mouth of death, what obstacle is yours? They have entered it themselves.
sanskrit_cite: ata ubhayorapi jñānājñānayormadhyagaḥ śrībhagavatānuśiṣyate   śrībhagavānuvāca   tvaṃ mānuṣyeṇopahatāntarātmā viṣādamohābhibhavādvisaṃjñaḥ | kṛpāgṛhītaḥ samavekṣya bandhū- bhiprapannānmukhamantakasya | mānuṣyaṃ-manuṣyabhāvaḥ | antakamukhaṃ svayamete praviṣṭā iti  tava ko bādhaḥ

plain_english: You grieve for what should not be grieved and do not speak like a wise person; learned ones do not grieve for the departed or the living. It is impossible to grieve for the body, since it is always perishable; and you grieve for the self, which is not worthy of grief. No one, whether dead or living, is to be grieved; for the self is indestructible, moving through various bodies, so what grief-worthiness is there? Nor is there grief-worthiness in the transfer of bodies; otherwise grief-worthiness would arise even in youth and so on.
sanskrit_cite: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñavannābhibhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ | śocitumaśakyaṃ kalevaraṃ-sadā naśvaratvāt aśocanārhamātmānaṃ  ca śocasi | na kaścit gatāsuḥ - mṛtaḥ agatāsuḥ - jīvanvā  śocyo'sti | tathāhi-ātmā tāvadavināśī nānāśarīreṣu  saṃcarataḥ kāsya śocyatā | na ca dehantarasaṃcāre eva śocyatā | evaṃ hi yauvanādāvapi śocyatā bhavet

plain_english: Thus the two meanings are stated: I never was not, nor were you or these lords; we all shall be beyond this.
sanskrit_cite: evamarthadvayamāha   nahyevāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ | na caiva na  bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamitaḥ param

plain_english: As the embodied self passes through childhood, youth, and old age, so it passes to another body; the steady one is not deluded.
sanskrit_cite: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā  dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati | ahaṃ hi naiva nāsam api tu āsam | evaṃ tvam amī ca rājānaḥ | ākārāntare ca sati yadi śocyatā tarhi kaumārāt yauvanāvāptau  kimiti na śocyate | yo dhīraḥ sa na śocati | dhairyaṃ ca  etaccharīre'pi yasyāsthā nāsti tena sukaram | atastvaṃ  dhairyamanviccha | adhīrāstu mātrāśabdavācyairarthairye kṛtāḥ sparśā

plain_english: Sense contacts through the senses produce impermanent states; endure them, Bharata.
sanskrit_cite: indriyadvāreṇātmanā saṃbandhāḥ tatkṛtā yāḥ  śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhādyāvasthā anityāḥ tāsvapi śocanti | na  tvevaṃ dhīrā ityāha   mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata | athavā-mātrābhiḥ-indriyairyeṣāṃ sparśoṃ na tu  sākṣātparamātmanā | āgamaḥ-utpattiḥ | apāyo-vināśaḥ | etadyukrāṃstitikṣasva-sahasva

plain_english: The person whom these contacts do not disturb, steady in pain and pleasure, is fit for immortality.
sanskrit_cite: yaṃ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha | samaduḥkhasukhaṃ dhīraṃ so'mṛtatvāya kalpate | nanu yata evāgamāpāyina ete sarve daśāviśeṣāstata eva śocyante  ? maivam | tathāhi ko'yamāgamo nāma ? utpattiriti cet | sāpi kā ?  asata ātmalābhaḥ sā iti tvasat | asatsvabhāvatā hi  niḥsvabhāvatā nirātmatā | nirātmā ca niḥsvabhāvaḥ kathaṃ sa  svabhāvīkartuṃ śakyaḥ anīlaṃ hi na nīlīkartuṃ  śakyam-svabhāvāntarāpatterduṣṭatvāt | tathā ca śāstram   nahi svabhāvo bhāvānāṃ vyāvartetauṣṇyavadraveḥ | iti | atha sata evātmalābha utpattiḥ tadā labdhātmano'sya jātvapi  anabhāvāt nityataivetyāgame kā śocyatā | evamapāyo'pi sato'sato  vā | asattāvadasadeva | satsvabhāvasyāpi kathamasattāsvabhāvaḥ | dvitīye kṣaṇe'sāvasatsvabhāvaḥ-iti cet ādye'pi tathā syāditi  na kaścidbhāvaḥ syāt svabhāvasyātyāgāt | atha mudgarādināsya

plain_english: Non-being has no being, and being has no non-being; truth-seers see the end of both.
sanskrit_cite: nāśaḥ kriyate | sa yadi vyatiriktaḥ bhāvasya kiṃ vṛttam ? na  dṛśyate-iti cet mā nāma darśi bhāvaḥ | na tvanyathābhūtaḥ  paṭāvṛta iva | avyatiriktastu nāsāvityuktam | tadetatsaṃkṣipyāha   nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ | ubhayorapi  dṛṣṭo'ntastvanayostattvadarśibhiḥ | atha ca lokavṛttenedamāha-asato-nityavināśinaḥ śarīrasya na  bhāvaḥ-anavaratamavasthābhiḥ pariṇāmitvāt | nityasataśca-paramātmano nāsti  kadācidvināśo'pariṇāmadharmatvāt | tathā ca vedaḥ   avināśī vā are'yamātmānucchittidharmā iti | (bṛ0 ā0 4 | 14)   anayoḥ sadasatorantaḥ-pratiṣṭhāpadaṃ yatrānayorviśrāntiḥ

plain_english: Know that as indestructible by which all this is pervaded; no one can destroy the imperishable.
sanskrit_cite: yastattvadarśibhidṛṣṭaḥ sa khalu nityo'nityo vā-ityāśaṅkyāha   avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṃ tatam | vināśamavyayasyāsya  na kaścitkartumarhati | tuścārthe | ātmā ca avināśī | tuścārthe | ātmā ca  avināśī

plain_english: These bodies are finite, while the embodied self is eternal and immeasurable; therefore fight without grief.
sanskrit_cite: antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ | vināśino'prameyasya tasmādyuddhyasva bhārata | nirupākhyatākāle sthūlavināśayoginaḥ tadanyathānupapattereva ca  vināśinaḥ-pratikṣaṇamavasthāntarabhāginaḥ | yaduktaṃ   ante purāṇatāṃ dṛṣṭvā pratikṣaṇaṃ navatvahāniranumīyate | iti | munināpi   kalānāṃ pṛthagarthānāṃ pratibhedaḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe | vartate  sarvabhāveṣu saukṣmyāttu na vibhāvyate | iti | pṛthagarthānāmiti-pṛthagarthakriyākāritvāditi yāvat | dehā antavanto vināśinaśca | ātmā tu nityaḥ yato'prameyaḥ | prameyasya tu jaḍasya pariṇāmitvaṃ na tvajaḍasya cidekarūpasya  svabhāvāntarāyogāt | evaṃ dehā nityamantavantaḥ iti  śocitumaśakyāḥ | ātmā nityamavināśī tena na śocanārhaḥ | tantreṇāyamakeḥ kṛtyapratyayo dvayorarthayormuninā darśita  aśocyān iti

plain_english: The self neither slays nor is slain; one who thinks otherwise is ignorant and bound.
sanskrit_cite: ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaścainaṃ manyate hatam | ubhau tau na  vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate | ya enamātmānaṃ dehaṃ ca hantāraṃ hataṃ ca vetti tasya ajñānam  ata eva sa baddhaḥ

plain_english: The self is unborn, eternal, and not slain when the body is slain.
sanskrit_cite: na jāyate mriyate vā kadāci- nnāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na  bhūyaḥ | ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne  śarīre | etadeva sphuṭayati-nāyaṃ bhūtvā-iti | ayamātmā na na bhūtvā  bhavitā apitu bhūtvaiva | ato na jāyate | na ca mriyate-yato bhūtvā  na na bhavitā apitu bhavitaiva

plain_english: One who knows the indestructible self neither slays nor is slain, so how is there bondage?
sanskrit_cite: vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enamajamavyayam | kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ  pārtha hanyate hanti vā katham | ya enamātmānaṃ prabuddhatvājjānāti na sa hanti na sa hanyate iti  tasya kathaṃ bandhaḥ

plain_english: As worn garments are discarded and new ones taken, so the embodied self takes new bodies.
sanskrit_cite: vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro'parāṇi | tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇā- nyanyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī | yathā vastrācchāditastadvastranāśe samucitavastrāntarāvṛto na  vinaśyati evamātmā dehāntarāvṛtaḥ

plain_english: Weapons, fire, water, and wind do not destroy the self.
sanskrit_cite: nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ | na cainaṃ  kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ

plain_english: This Self cannot be cut, burned, wetted, or dried; it is eternal, all-pervading, immovable, and everlasting.
sanskrit_cite: acchedyo'yamadāhyo'yamakledyo'śoṣya eva ca | nityaḥ sarvagataḥ  sthāṇuracalo'yaṃ sanātanaḥ

plain_english: This Self is unmanifest, inconceivable, and unmodifiable; therefore, having known it, one should not grieve. No weapon or other cause can destroy him, since he is of one conscious nature, independent, partless, and free, and cannot be destroyed by another nature, dependence, destruction of parts, or division. Nor is his going to another body something new: even while embodied he always goes to another body, and therefore he is connected. Since a body does not remain even for a moment, having known this Self thus, one should not grieve.
sanskrit_cite: avyakto'yamacintyo'yamavikāryo'yamucyate | tasmādevaṃ viditvainaṃ  nānuśocitumarhasi | nāsya nāśakāraṇaṃ śastrādi kiṃcitkaram  cidekasvabhāvasyānāśritasya nirapekṣasya niraṃśasya svataṃtrasya  svabhāvāntarāpattyāśrayavināśāvayavavibhāgavirodhiprādurbhāva  adi-krameṇa nāśayitumaśakyatvāt | na ca  dehāntaragamanamasyāpūrvam | dehānvito'pi satataṃ dehāntaraṃ  gacchati tena saṃvadhyata ityarthaḥ dehasya  kṣaṇamātramapyanavasthāyitvāt | evaṃbhūtaṃ viditvainamātmānaṃ  śocituṃ nārhasi

plain_english: Even if you regard him as ever-born or dead, O mighty-armed, you should not grieve for him. Even if you regard the body as ever-born through an unbroken stream, there is no ground for grief through a momentary process; even if it is ever-perishing, what grief is there? Thus, if you think the self's union with or separation from that body makes it ever-born or ever-dead, grieving is in every way unfitting for knowers.
sanskrit_cite: athavainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam | tathāpi tvaṃ  mahābāho nainaṃ śocitumarhasi | athāpyenaṃ dehaṃ manyase nityajātaṃ pravāhasyāvināśāt tathāpi  na śocyatā | kṣaṇikaprakriyayā vā nityavināśinam tathāpi kā  śocyatā | evaṃ yadi ātmanastaddehasaṃyogaviyogābhyāṃ  nityajātatvaṃ nityamṛtatvaṃ vā manyase tathāpi sarvathā śocanaṃ  prāmāṇikānāmayuktam

plain_english: Since birth and death are inevitable and form a wheel, one should not grieve.
sanskrit_cite: na caitadanyathā nityatvānityatvamupapattimat-yataḥ   jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca | tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi | janmana evānantaraṃ nāśo nāśādanantaraṃ janma iti cakravadayaṃ  janmamaraṇasantāna iti kiṃ parimāṇaṃ śocyatāmiti

plain_english: Since beings are unmanifest before and after, and change is only modification, there is no cause for lamentation.
sanskrit_cite: apica   avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata | avyaktanidhanānyeva  tatra kā paridevanā | nityāḥ santu anityā vā yastāvadasya śocakastaṃ pratyeva  ādāvavyaktaḥ ante cāvyaktaḥ madhyetasya vyaktatā vikāra iti  pratyuta vikāre śocanīyaṃ na svabhāve | kiṃca  yattanmūlakāraṇaṃ kiṃcidabhimataṃ tadeva yathākramaṃ  vicitrasvabhāvatayā svātmamadhye  darśitatattadanantasṛṣṭisthitisaṃhṛtivaicitryaṃ nityameva | tathāsvabhāve'pi kāsya śocyatā

plain_english: The self is a wonder: some see it, some speak of it, some hear yet do not know it.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃvidhaṃ ca   āścaryavat paśyati kaścidena- māścaryavadvadati tathainamanyaḥ | āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit | nanu yadyevamayamātmā avināśī kimiti sarveṇa tathaiva nopalabhyate  ? yato'dbhutavatkaścideva paśyati | śrutvāpi na kaścidenaṃ  jānāti-vetti

plain_english: The embodied self is eternally indestructible in every body, Bharata; therefore you should not grieve for any beings, since the self's indestructibility is eternal.
sanskrit_cite: dehī nityamavadhyo'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata | tasmātsarvāṇi  bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi | ato nityamātmano'vināśitvam

plain_english: Considering even your own duty, you should not waver; for a kshatriya no better righteous duty than war is found, and since own duty is non-removable, trembling about war is unfitting.
sanskrit_cite: svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi | dharmyāddhi  yuddhācchreyo'nyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate | svadharmasya cānapahāryatvāt yuddhaviṣayaḥ kampo na yuktaḥ

plain_english: By chance such war arrives with heaven's gate opened; meritorious kshatriyas obtain it, Partha. Even desire-filled kshatriyas should not abandon such war because it causes heaven; how much less one to whom such knowledge is taught. The verse's purport is not merely ending in heaven.
sanskrit_cite: yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāramapāvṛtam | sukṛtātkṣatriyāḥ  pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam | anye'pi ye kāmamayāḥ kṣatriyāstairapi īdṛśaṃ yuddhaṃ  svargahetutvānna tyājyam kiṃ punaryasya īdṛśaṃ  jñānamupadiṣṭamiti tātparyam | na punaḥ svargaparyavasāyī  ślokaḥ

plain_english: The fear from which you would turn from war will itself fall upon you in a hundred branches. If you do not fight this righteous battle, then abandoning your own duty and fame you will obtain sin.
sanskrit_cite: yadbhayācca bhavān yuddhānnivarteta tadeva  śataśākhamupanipatiṣyati bhavata ityāha   atha cettvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi | tataḥ  svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi

plain_english: Beings will also speak your ill-fame; for an esteemed imperishable one, ill-fame surpasses death.
sanskrit_cite: akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te'vyayām | sambhāvitasya  cākīrtirmaraṇādatiricyate

plain_english: Great charioteers will think you retreated from battle out of fear; having been highly regarded by them, you will go to lightness in their eyes.
sanskrit_cite: bhayādraṇāduparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ | yeṣāṃ ca  tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam

plain_english: Your enemies will speak many unspeakable words and blame your power; what pain could be greater than that?
sanskrit_cite: avācyavādāṃśca bahūnvadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ | nindantastava  sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim

plain_english: Slain, you gain heaven; victorious, you enjoy earth; therefore rise, son of Kunti, resolved for battle.
sanskrit_cite: hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm | tasmāduttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ | ślokapañcakamidamabhyupagamya vādarūpamucyate yadi laukikena  vyavahāreṇāste bhavāṃstathāpyavaśyānuṣṭheyametat

plain_english: Having made pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat equal, engage in battle; thus you will not incur sin.
sanskrit_cite: sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau | tato yuddhāya  yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi | tava tu svadharmatayaiva karmāṇi kurvato na kadācitpāpasambandhaḥ

plain_english: This wisdom was told in Sankhya; hear how, endowed with it, you abandon action-bondage in yoga.
sanskrit_cite: eṣā te'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṃ śṛṇu | buddhyā  yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi | eṣā ca tava sāṃkhye-samyagjñāne buddhiḥ-niścayātmikā uktā | eṣaiva ca yathā yoge-karmakauśale yojyate tathaiva śṛṇu | yayā  buddhyā karmaṇāṃ bandhakatvaṃ tyakṣyasi | nahi karmāṇi svayaṃ  badhnanti-jaḍatvāt ataḥ svayamātmā  karmabhirvāsanātmakairātmānaṃ badhnāti

plain_english: Even a little of this duty protects from great fear; even small yoga-wisdom destroys samsara-fear.
sanskrit_cite: nehātikramanāśo'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate | svalpamapyasya  dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt | asyāṃ buddhau atikrameṇa-aparādhena pramādena nāśo na  bhavati-pramādasyābhāvāt | yathā ca parimitena śrīkhaṇḍakaṇena  jvālāyamāno'pi tailakaṭāhaḥ sadyaḥ śītībhavati evamanayā  svalpayāpi yogabuddhyā mahābhayaṃ saṃsārarūpaṃ vinaśyati

plain_english: This wisdom is not newly brought; resolute wisdom is one, while unresolved wisdoms are many-branched and endless.
sanskrit_cite: na caiṣā buddhirapūrvānīyate kiṃtarhi   vyavasāyātmikā buddhirekaiva kurunandana | bahuśākhā hyanantāśca  buddhayo'vyavasāyinām | vyavasāyātmikā sarvasyaikaiva sahajā dhīḥ | niścetavyavaśāttu  bahutvaṃ gacchati

plain_english: Thus fools speak this flowery speech, attached to Vedic debate, O Partha, claiming nothing else exists.
sanskrit_cite: tathāca   yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadantyavipaścitaḥ | vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastītivādinaḥ

plain_english: Desire-natured, heaven-focused, desiring fruits of birth and action, full of special rites, they follow paths toward enjoyment and power.
sanskrit_cite: kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalepsavaḥ | kriyāviśeṣabahulā bhogaiśvaryagatīḥ prati

plain_english: For minds stolen by that speech, resolute understanding is not given in concentration; desire-craving speakers praise flowery Vedic speech filled with future heaven-fruit, desire fruit from action, and even with resolute understanding are not fit for concentration because of fruit-certainty; this is the purport of the three verses.
sanskrit_cite: bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām | vyavasāyātmikā  buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate | ye kāmābhilāṣiṇaste svayametāṃ vācaṃ vedātmikāṃ  puṣpitāṃ-bhaviṣyatsvargaphalena vyāptāṃ vadanti | ata eva  janmanaḥ karmaiva phalamicchanti te'vapiścitaḥ | te ca  tayaiva-svayaṃkalpitayā vedavācā apahṛtacittā  vyavasāyabuddhiyuktā api na samādhiyogyāḥ-tatra  phalaniścayatvāditi ślokatrayasya tātparyam

plain_english: Therefore the Vedas concern the three strands; be beyond them, Arjuna, beyond pairs, established in constant being, free from acquisition and security, self-possessed. The Vedas bind by three-stranded instrument especially, not as binders by nature, because Vedic actions done with pleasure-pain-delusion understanding are binding; therefore desire-form three-strandedness is to be abandoned. If this were Veda-criticism, the matter of doing battle would be obstructed, for lack of certainty of own duty without Veda; but for those whose desire for fruit has fallen away, the Vedas are not binders.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva ca   traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna | nirdvandvo  nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān | vedāstraiguṇyena karaṇena viśeṣeṇa sinvanti-badhnanti na tu  bandhakāḥ | yasmāt sukhaduḥkhamohabuddhyā karmāṇi vaidikāni  kriyamāṇāni bandhakāni atastraiguṇyaṃ-kāmarūpaṃ tyājyam | yadi  tu vedadūṣaṇaparametadabhaviṣyat prakṛtaṃ yuddhakaraṇaṃ  vyaghaṭiṣyata-vedādanyasya svadharmaniścāyakatvābhāvāt | yeṣāṃ tu phalābhilāṣo vigalitasteṣāṃ na vedā bandhakāḥ

plain_english: Because the Vedas are supreme for those fit for right knowing, therefore he says: as much purpose as in a well, so much in all Vedas for the knowing brahmin; for one whose primacy is in own duty and knowing, even limited Veda-spoken work is to be done.
sanskrit_cite: yato vedāḥ paraṃ teṣāṃ samyagjñānopayoginaḥ ata āha   yāvānartha udapāne sarvataḥ samplutodake | tāvānsarveṣu vedeṣu  brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ | yasya svadharmamātre jñāne ca prādhānyaṃ parimitādapi  vedabhāṣitātkāryam

plain_english: Therefore your right is in action, never in fruits; do not be cause of action-fruit, and let no attachment be in inaction. Be engaged in action only, not in fruits. Surely action done necessarily brings fruit? Not so: if you are pervaded by fruit-desire impurity, then action becomes cause of fruit; unasked fruit is knowing, not for the unwilling. Attachment through absence of action is firm-grasp false knowing, to be abandoned indeed.
sanskrit_cite: ataśca   karmaṇyastvadhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana | mā  karmaphalahetubhūrmā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi | karmamātre tvaṃ vyāpṛto bhava natu karmaphaleṣu | nanu karmaṇi  kṛte nāntarīyakatayaiva phalamāpatati iti ? maivam | tatra hi yadi  tvaṃ phalakāmanā-kāluṣyavyāpto bhavasi tadā karmaṇāṃ phalaṃ  prati hetutvam | yadaprārthyamānaṃ phalaṃ tat jñānam | nānicchostaditi karmābhāvena yaḥ saṅgaḥ sa eva gāḍhagraharūpo  mithyā-jñānasvarūpaḥ iti tyājya eva

plain_english: Established in yoga, do actions abandoning attachment; equality in success and failure is yoga.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃtarhi   yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañjaya | siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate | yoge sthitvā karmāṇi kuru | sāmyaṃ ca yogaḥ

plain_english: One whose undertakings are free from desire-bonds is the wise renouncer; longing binds.
sanskrit_cite: yasya sarve samārambha nirāśīrbandhanāstviha | tyāge yasya hutaṃ  sarvaṃ sa tyāgī sa ca buddhimān | yasya sarve vyāpārā āśīrūpeṇa bandhanena na yuktāḥ | abhilāṣo hi bandhakaḥ

plain_english: Action is far inferior to yoga of wisdom; seek refuge in intellect, for wretched fruit-causers remain distant.
sanskrit_cite: dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanañjaya | buddhau  śaraṇamanviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ | buddhiyogātkila hetoravaraṃ-duṣṭaphalaṃ riktaṃ karma dūrībhavati | atastādṛśyāṃ buddhau śaraṇamanviccha-prārthayasva yena sā  buddhirlabhyate

plain_english: Joined to intellect, one abandons both good and bad deeds; yoga is skill in actions.
sanskrit_cite: buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte | tasmādyogāya yujyasva  yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam | ubhe iti parasparavyabhicāraṃ darśayati | tasmāt-yathāhi  sukṛttaduṣkṛte naśyatastathākaraṇameva paramaṃ kauśalamiti  bhāvaḥ

plain_english: Wise ones, abandoning action-born fruit, are freed from birth-bond and attain the unailing state.
sanskrit_cite: karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ | janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchantyanāmayam | yogabuddhiyuktāḥ karmaṇāṃ phalaṃ tyaktvā janmabandhaṃ  tyajantibrahmasattāmavāpnuvanti

plain_english: When your intellect crosses the delusion-thicket, then you will go to weariness of what is to be heard and heard.
sanskrit_cite: yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhirvyatitariṣyati | tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ  śrotavyasya śrutasya ca

plain_english: When your intellect stands unmoving in samadhi, you will attain yoga; then recognition becomes clear and dispassion follows.
sanskrit_cite: śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā | samādhāvacalā  buddhistadā yogamavāpsyasi | tatra ca yogabuddhiprāptyavasare va sphuṭamevedamabhijñānam  śrotavyasya śrutasyābhilaṣyamāṇasya ca āgamasya ubhayasyāpi  nirvedabhāktvam | anena  cedamuktam-avidyāpadanipatitapramātranugrāhakaśāstraśravaṇasaṃsk  āra-vipralambhamahimā ayaṃ - yattavāsthāne  kulakṣayādidoṣadarśanam tattu tathā śāsanabahumānavigalane  vigaliṣyatīti

plain_english: Arjuna asks what speech, sitting, and going characterize steady wisdom in samadhi.
sanskrit_cite: arjuna uvāca   sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava | sthiradhīḥ  kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajecca kim | yadā sthāsyati buddhiḥ-ityanena vacasā samādhisthasya yogino yaḥ  sthitaprajñaśabdastatra vācaka uktastasya kā bhāṣā-kiṃ  pravṛttinimittaṃ bhāṣyate yena nimittena śabdairartha iti kṛtvā  yoginaḥ sthitaprajñaśabdaḥ kiṃ rūḍhyā vācako'nvarthatayā vā  iti ekaḥ praśnaḥ | yadyapi rūḍhau śaṅkaiva nāsti  tathāpyanvarthatāṃ labdhāmapi svarūpalakṣaṇanimittanirūpaṇena  sphuṭīkartumeṣa praśnaḥ | sthiradhīriti  śabdapadārthako'rthapadārthakaśca tatra sthiradhīśabdaḥ kiṃ  prayogalakṣaṇamevārthamāha āho tapasvinamapi iti dvitīyaḥ  praśnaḥ | sa ca sthiradhīryogī kimāsīt-kimabhyasyet-kvāsya  sthairyaṃ syāt iti tṛtīyaḥ | abhyasyaṃśca kimāpnuyāt iti  caturthaḥ

plain_english: When one abandons all desires and is content in the self, steady wisdom is declared.
sanskrit_cite: etadeva praśnacatuṣṭayaṃ krameṇa nirṇīyate śrībhagavatā   śrī bhagavānuvāca   prajahāti yadā kāmānsarvānpārtha manogatān | ātmanyevātmanā  tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate | sthitā rūḍhā prajñā  yasya | rūḍhiśca nityamātmarūḍhitve sati viṣayavikṣepakṛtasya  kāmarūpasya bhramasya nivṛttatvāt yogino yaḥ  sthitaprajña-śabdo'nvarthaḥ sa cetthaṃyukta ityekaḥ praśno  nirṇītaḥ

plain_english: Unagitated in suffering, desireless in pleasure, free from attachment, fear, and anger, such a sage is steady-minded.
sanskrit_cite: duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ | vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthiradhīrmunirucyate | sukhaduḥkhayoryasya rāgadveṣarahitā vṛttiḥ sa munireva  sthiraprajño nānyaḥ

plain_english: Fitting, because one unattached everywhere, obtaining good or bad, neither rejoices nor hates, and wisdom is established.
sanskrit_cite: yuktaṃ caitat yataḥ   yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham | nābhinandati na  dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā | śubhāśubhaprāptau tasyāhlādatāpau na bhavataḥ

plain_english: When one withdraws the senses from objects like a tortoise, steady wisdom is declared.
sanskrit_cite: yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ | indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyaḥ sthiraprajñastadocyate | na cāsya pācakavadyogarūḍhitvam yadā yadā kilāyamindriyāṇi  saṃharate-ātmanyeva kūrma ivāṅgāni kroḍīkaroti viṣayibhyo  viṣayānnivārya tadā tadā sthiraprajñaḥ | yadvā-indriyārthebhyaḥ prabhṛti indriyāṇi ātmani  saṃharate-viṣayendriyādikaṃ sarvamātmasātkaroti | nanu tapasvino'pi kathaṃ sthiraprajñaśabdo na pravartate ? ucyate-

plain_english: Objects withdraw from one who fasts, but taste remains; seeing the supreme removes that residue, so only the yogin is steady in wisdom.
sanskrit_cite: viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ | rasavarjaṃ raso'pyasya  paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate | yadyapi āhāryaiḥ-rūpādibhirviṣayaiḥ saṃbandho'sya nāsti  tathāpi tasya viṣayā antaḥkaraṇagatamuparāgalakṣaṇaṃ rasaṃ  varjayitvā nivartante | ato nāsau sthiraprajñaḥ | yoginastu  parameśvaradarśanāduparāgo na bhavati anyasya tu tapasvino nāsau  nivartate

plain_english: Even a wise person's mind is seized by turbulent senses, so the yogin must conquer the mind.
sanskrit_cite: yattasyāpi hi kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ | indriyāṇi  pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ | yat-yasmāt tasyāpi-tapasvino mana indriyairhiyate athavā  yattasya-sayatnasyāpi | yoginā ca mana eva jetavyam iti dvitīyo  nirṇītaḥ

plain_english: Having restrained the senses by mind, one should sit devoted to me; wisdom is established when senses are controlled.
sanskrit_cite: tāni saṃyamya manasā yukta āsīta matparaḥ | vaśe hi  yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā | ya evaṃ manasā indriyāṇi niyamayati natu apravṛttyā sa eva  sthiraprajñaḥ | sa ca matpara evāsīta-māmeva cidātmānaṃ  parameśvaraṃ abhyasyet

plain_english: For one meditating on objects, attachment arises; from attachment desire, and from desire anger.
sanskrit_cite: dhyāyato viṣayānpuṃsaḥ saṅgasteṣūpajāyate | saṅgāt  sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmātkrodho'bhijāyate

plain_english: Anger leads to delusion, memory confusion, intellect destruction, and ruin; mere renunciation ends in grasping, so it is not the means for steady wisdom.
sanskrit_cite: krodhādbhavati sammohaḥ sammohātsmṛtivibhramaḥ | smṛtibhraṃśādbuddhināśo buddhināśāt praṇaśyati | tapasvino viṣayatyāga eva viṣayagrahaṇe paryavasyati | dhyātvā hi  te tyajyante | dhyānakāla eva ca saṅgādaya upajāyante-ityanupāyo  viṣayatyāgaḥ sthiraprajñasya

plain_english: Freed from attachment and aversion, moving through objects with controlled senses, the self-controlled one attains serenity.
sanskrit_cite: rāgadveṣavimuktaistu viṣayānindriyaiścaran | ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati

plain_english: In calmness, loss of all sorrows arises for him; indeed quickly the intellect of the clear-minded one becomes established.
sanskrit_cite: prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānirasyopajāyate | prasannacetaso hyāśu  buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate

plain_english: There is no intellect for the unyoked one, nor meditation for the unyoked one, nor peace for the unpeaceful one; whence happiness?
sanskrit_cite: nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktamya bhāvanā | na cābhāvayataḥ  śāntiraśāntasya kutaḥ sukham

plain_english: Indeed, of the roaming senses, the mind that follows them carries away his wisdom, as wind carries a boat on water.
sanskrit_cite: indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yanmano'nuvidhīyate | tadasya harati  prajñāṃ vāyurnāvamivāmbhasi

plain_english: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, whose senses are wholly restrained from sense-objects, his wisdom is established; but one who controls the mind, even while serving objects, is not overwhelmed by waves of anger and the like; thus he alone is the steady-wisdom yogi—this is the purport.
sanskrit_cite: tasmādyasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ | indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā | yastu manaso niyāmakaḥ sa viṣayānsevamāno'pi na  krodhādikallolairabhibhūyate iti sa eva sthiraprajño yogī-iti  tātparyam

plain_english: The yogi, though performing all practical dealings, is transcendent; the supreme Lord, having summarized his own nature, tells it: the night of all beings is the sage's waking; the night in which beings wake is the sage's night; how is this maya, the deluding night of all beings, to be abandoned? In the state where the world wakes and performs various activities, that is the sage's night, because he is unawakened to practical dealing. This is said: this maya indeed has deluding nature, name-and-form, and appearance of dependence on pleasure; there the world, without touching her original own-nature, sits bound in memory in the second form. The yogi, however, is opposite: he sees her deluding nature for uprooting it, and does not regard dependence on pleasure; seeing rightly, the knower disregards dependence on pleasure through destruction of false knowledge. See indeed, that is night—wonder! In knowledge the yogi attends where all are deluded; in ignorance, however, where a person is unawakened, there he is awakened—also wonder.
sanskrit_cite: yogī ca sarvavyavahārān kurvāṇo'pi lokottaraḥ-iti nirūpayatā  parameśvareṇa saṃkṣipyāsya svarūpaṃ kathyate   yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī | yasyāṃ  jāgrati bhūtāni sā rātriḥ paśyato muneḥ | yā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ niśā-mohanī māyā tasyāṃ  munirjāgarti-kathamiyaṃ heyeti | yasyāṃ ca daśāyāṃ loko  jāgarti-nānāvidhāṃ ceṣṭāṃ kurute sā muneḥ rātriḥ yato'sau  vyavahāraṃ pratyabuddhaḥ | etaduktaṃ bhavati-yeyaṃ māyā khalu  tasyā mohakatvaṃ nāmarūpaṃ sukhatantratābhāsanaṃ ca | tatra-lokaḥ prācyaṃ svarūpamasyā aparāmṛśyaiva dvitīyasminrūpe  nibaddhasmṛtirāste | yogī tu tadviparītastadīyaṃ mohakatvaṃ  tadunmūlanāya paśyati sukhatantratāṃ tu nādriyate | paśyan  samyagjñānī mithyājñānopaghātācca sukhatantratānādaraḥ | paśyata eva sā rātririti citram | vidyāyāṃ cāvadhatte yogī yatra  sarvo vimūḍhaḥ | avidyāyāṃ tvabuddhaḥ yatra janaḥ  prabuddhaḥ-ityapi citram

plain_english: Therefore indeed, just as waters enter the ocean that is being filled yet remains immovably established, so all desires enter him; he attains peace, not the desire-desiring one. The yogi does not run outward even for desire's sake; but by sense-nature, objects entering after him do not make waves, like river currents into the ocean. Thus the third is decided.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva   āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat | tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī | yogī na kāmārthaṃ bahirdhāvati api tvindriyadharmatayā | taṃ  viṣayā anupraviśanto na taraṅgayanti nadīvegā ivodadhim | evaṃ  tṛtīyo nirṇītaḥ

plain_english: Having abandoned all desires, the desireless, selfless, egoless man walks and attains peace; that yogi, through renunciation of all desires, reaches liberation in the form of peace.
sanskrit_cite: vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvānpumāṃścarati nispṛhaḥ | nirmamo  nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntimadhigacchati | sa yogī sarvakāmasaṃnyāsitvāt śāntirūpaṃ mokṣameti

plain_english: This is the brahmic state, Partha; having reached it one is not deluded, and even at the end one reaches brahma-nirvana. This brahma-being, in which even a moment's stability, once obtained, leads from body-breaking to supreme brahman, is thus the resolution of the four questions; auspicious.
sanskrit_cite: eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati | sthitvāsyāmantakāle'pi brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati | eṣāsau brahmasattā yasyāṃ kṣaṇamātraṃ sthitvā-avasthitiṃ  prāpya śarīrabhedāt paramaṃ brahmāpnoti iti praśnacatuṣṭayaṃ  nirṇītamiti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: ah, indeed the mind's wondrous course ascends by abandonment; taking refuge in objects, one should abandon them. Thus in the Gita-meaning-gathering composed by Abhinavagupta, the second chapter.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   aho nu cetasaścitrā gatistyāgena yatkila | ārohatyeva  viṣayāñchrayaṃstāṃstu parityajet | iti  śrīmahāmāheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ
